title: ExtraTrees + CatBoost + MLP equal rank blend
spec: Build a three-member rank-averaged ensemble out of the three model families that have each scored at or below the incumbent on their own. Member 1: ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=800, max_features=0.5, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) on the current descriptor+pharmacophore matrix. Member 2: CatBoostClassifier(iterations=600, depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0) on the same matrix. Member 3: the existing 5-seed MLPClassifier ensemble on the quantile-normal transform. Rank-normalize each member's probabilities and average with equal weights 1/3. Drop the RandomForest entirely. Keep total runtime under 10 minutes; if CatBoost is slow, reduce it to 400 iterations.

title: Tanimoto kNN as rank-blend member
spec: Add a k-nearest-neighbour classifier on binary Morgan radius-2 2048-bit fingerprints using Tanimoto similarity (computed as intersection / union from a dense 0/1 matrix product). For each test molecule, take the k=10 most similar training molecules and predict the similarity-weighted fraction of positives (weights = similarity**3, fallback 0.5 if all weights are zero). Rank-normalise its output and add it as a third member, with weights 1/3 each, to the existing RF and MLP rank blend. Keep all other code unchanged.

title: Pairwise ranking LightGBM as blend member
spec: Add a LightGBM ranker (objective='lambdarank' or 'rank_xendcg', one query group containing all training rows, 300 trees, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 10, colsample 0.3) trained on the same descriptor plus pharmacophore matrix. Its raw scores approximate pairwise AUROC-style ordering, which matches the metric. Rank-normalise its test scores and average them with the RF and MLP ranks with equal weights 1/3 each. Keep everything else unchanged.

title: ExtraTrees plus log1p Morgan counts
spec: Combine the two most promising single findings so far into one configuration. (a) In featurize, append a radius-2 Morgan count fingerprint folded to 1024 columns, transformed with log1p, to the existing RDKit descriptor block and Gobbi pharmacophore block (use rdkit.Chem.rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=1024).GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy, cast to float, then np.log1p). (b) Replace the RandomForestClassifier with ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=1000, max_features=0.5, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed). Keep the 5-seed MLP on the quantile-normal transform of the same (now wider) matrix and keep the 0.5/0.5 rank-average blend unchanged. Watch runtime: 15 fits must finish well inside 10 minutes, so if needed keep the MLP at 5 seeds and max_iter=200 as now.

title: Blend weight chosen by inner scaffold-grouped CV
spec: Replace the hard-coded 0.5/0.5 rank average with a weight picked from the training fold. Inside fit_predict, run an inner 4-fold GroupKFold over the training molecules, grouped by Murcko scaffold (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, falling back to the SMILES string when it fails), to collect out-of-fold RF and MLP scores (use 2 MLP seeds inside the inner loop to stay fast). Pick w from the grid 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 that maximizes inner AUROC of w * rank(RF) + (1 - w) * rank(MLP), then refit both models on the full training fold (5 MLP seeds as now) and return the blend with that w. Keep features and models unchanged and make sure the inner loop keeps 15 fits under 10 minutes.

title: Scaffold-grouped validation split for MLP early stopping
spec: The MLPs currently early-stop on a random 10 percent of the training fold, which shares ring skeletons with the training rows and therefore gives an optimistic, scaffold-leaky stopping signal. Replace this with a scaffold-disjoint hold-out. Compute the Murcko scaffold SMILES of every training molecule (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, falling back to the empty string on failure), then use sklearn.model_selection.GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.15, random_state=seed) grouped on scaffold to split the training fold into an inner-train and an inner-validation part. Train each of the 5 MLPs with early_stopping=False on the inner-train part while manually monitoring validation AUROC: simplest clean implementation is to use warm_start=True with max_iter=1 inside a loop of up to 150 epochs, tracking inner-validation AUROC each epoch, and keeping the predictions from the epoch with the best validation AUROC (predict on test at that epoch). Average over 5 seeds, then rank-blend 50/50 with the unchanged RF.

title: Label-smoothed MLP via regression
spec: Replace the MLPClassifier with MLPRegressor trained on soft targets (y*0.9+0.05), using the same hidden sizes (256,64), alpha 1e-2 and early_stopping. Use 5 seeds and average the outputs. Rank-blend with the RF as before.

title: Kernel ridge regression on a Tanimoto kernel as a blend member
spec: Compute the Tanimoto kernel matrix on binary Morgan radius-2 bits for train-train and test-train pairs, using the intersection/union formula from dense 0/1 products. Fit sklearn KernelRidge with kernel='precomputed', alpha=1.0, on targets encoded as +1 for positives and -1 for negatives. Use the raw predictions for test molecules, rank-normalise them, and add them as a third member with weight 1/3 in the rank blend. Keep the RF and MLP unchanged. This is a regression-on-kernel variant, distinct from the earlier SVC.

title: Feature-bagged MLP subspaces
spec: Train 8 MLPs, each on a random 60% subset of the quantile-normal feature columns. Draw the subset with np.random.RandomState(seed+i). Average their probabilities, then rank-blend with the RF 50/50.

title: Adam MLP with a longer schedule
spec: Change the MLPs to learning_rate_init=3e-4, batch_size=64, n_iter_no_change=20, max_iter=400, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.15. Keep the (256,64) layers and alpha 1e-2, with 5 seeds. Keep the blend unchanged.

title: Transductive quantile transform fitted on train plus test
spec: The QuantileTransformer for the MLP is currently fitted on the training fold only, so the test fold (built from unseen ring skeletons, hence a shifted feature distribution) is mapped through quantiles it does not match. Fit the transform transductively instead: stack Xtr and Xte, call QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=min(1000, n_rows), random_state=seed).fit on the stacked matrix, then transform the train and test blocks separately for MLP training and prediction. Labels are never touched, so this uses only the test SMILES that the harness already passes in. Keep the RF on the raw feature matrix, keep the 5-seed MLP and the 0.5/0.5 rank average unchanged.

title: SVD-compressed pharmacophore block for the MLP
spec: The MLP currently sees ~2048 sparse pharmacophore columns alongside ~210 dense descriptors, which likely drowns the descriptors. Change only the MLP's input: split the feature matrix into the descriptor block and the pharmacophore block, fit TruncatedSVD(n_components=128, random_state=seed) on the training pharmacophore block, and build the MLP input as the quantile-normal-transformed descriptors concatenated with the SVD scores (standardized by the training mean/sd of the scores). Fit the TruncatedSVD and QuantileTransformer on the training fold only and apply them to the test fold. The RF keeps the full uncompressed matrix, and the final 0.5/0.5 rank average is unchanged.

title: Tanimoto-similarity kNN as a third blend member
spec: Add a purely instance-based member to the rank blend, which is structurally very different from the forest and the MLP and may add complementary signal on unseen scaffolds. Compute binary Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) for train and test molecules as a dense 0/1 uint8 matrix, then compute the full test-by-train Tanimoto similarity matrix with matrix algebra: inter = Xte @ Xtr.T, sim = inter / (popcount_te[:,None] + popcount_tr[None,:] - inter) with a small epsilon in the denominator. For each test molecule take its k=25 most similar training molecules and predict the similarity-weighted mean of their labels (weights = similarity cubed, to sharpen). Rank-normalize this prediction and average it with the rank-normalized RF and MLP predictions using weights 0.3 RF, 0.45 MLP, 0.25 kNN. This is cheap (a single 1300x300 matrix product per fold) so runtime should barely change.

title: Label-smoothed MLP trained as a regressor
spec: Soften the MLP's targets so it is not pushed to saturate on a small, scaffold-shifted dataset. Replace the 5 MLPClassifier fits with 5 MLPRegressor fits (same hidden_layer_sizes=(256, 64), alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True, max_iter=300, random_state=seed + i) trained on smoothed targets y_soft = 0.1 + 0.8 * y on the quantile-normal feature matrix. Average the 5 regression outputs; because only the ranking matters, use the raw averaged output directly as the MLP score. Rank-average it 0.5/0.5 with the unchanged RF probability exactly as the current script does.

title: Mixup augmentation for MLP training
spec: Before training each MLP member, create an augmented copy of the quantile-normal training matrix with 2x as many rows. Each new row is a convex combination of two random training rows, with mixing weight lam drawn from Beta(0.4, 0.4) per row (seeded by the seed argument). Its target is the same lam-weighted mix of the two 0/1 labels. Because MLPClassifier needs hard labels, train an MLPRegressor on the soft targets (clipped to [0,1]) with the same hidden sizes and alpha, and use its output clipped to [0,1] as the MLP score. Keep the 5-seed averaging and rank blend unchanged.

title: Replicate ExtraTrees in place of the RF
spec: Confirm the single best observed result by re-running it exactly: in fit_predict, replace RandomForestClassifier with ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=1000, max_features=0.5, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) and keep everything else identical (same featurize with descriptors + Gobbi pharmacophore bits, same 5-seed MLP on the quantile-normal matrix, same 0.5/0.5 rank average). Import ExtraTreesClassifier from sklearn.ensemble and leave the N_TREES/MAX_FEATURES constants wired to the new model so the file stays tidy. The only purpose of this job is a clean replicate of the 0.0890 observation, so change nothing else, and keep runtime similar to the current script (ExtraTrees with 1000 trees on ~4000 features is fast, well under the limit).

title: Rank blend weights tuned by inner CV
spec: Use an inner 3-fold StratifiedKFold on the training data to get out-of-fold RF and MLP predictions (use 2 MLP seeds to save time). Pick the blend weight w in {0.2,0.35,0.5,0.65,0.8} that maximizes inner OOF AUROC of the rank blend. Then fit on the full train fold and blend with w. Keep total runtime under 10 minutes.

title: L-BFGS MLP instead of Adam
spec: In the MLP member, change the solver from the default adam to lbfgs (MLPClassifier(solver='lbfgs', hidden_layer_sizes=(256,64), alpha=1e-2, max_iter=500)). Drop early_stopping and validation_fraction, which lbfgs does not use. Keep the 5-seed averaging and the quantile-normal inputs. Keep the RF and the rank blend unchanged. The aim is a deterministic full-batch optimiser that may fit small tabular data better than adam.

title: Bootstrap-bagged MLP ensemble
spec: Give the MLP half of the blend more variance reduction by bagging over data as well as over initialization. Replace the loop of 5 MLPClassifiers trained on the full training fold with a loop of 10 MLPClassifiers, where each one is fit on a bootstrap resample of the training rows (draw len(y) indices with replacement using np.random.default_rng(seed + i), and skip/redraw a resample that happens to contain only one class). Keep hidden_layer_sizes=(256, 64), alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True, max_iter=200, random_state=seed + i. Average the 10 predicted probabilities, then rank-average 0.5/0.5 with the unchanged RF as before.

title: SVD-compressed MLP input
spec: For the MLP branch only, apply TruncatedSVD (n_components=128, random_state=seed) to the quantile-normal matrix, fit on the train fold. Standardize the result and train the 5 MLPs on it. The RF still uses raw features. Rank-blend as before.

title: HistGradientBoosting as a third blend member
spec: Add sklearn's HistGradientBoostingClassifier, which has not been tried yet, as a third equally weighted member of the rank blend alongside the existing RF and 5-seed MLP. Use HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=400, learning_rate=0.05, max_leaf_nodes=31, min_samples_leaf=20, l2_regularization=1.0, early_stopping=False, random_state=seed) fitted on the same descriptor+pharmacophore matrix as the RF (it handles the many sparse binary pharmacophore columns natively and is fast on 8 threads). Rank-normalize all three prediction vectors with rankdata/len and average them with weights 1/3 each. Change nothing else.

title: Four-model rank average of the near-tied families
spec: Instead of picking between the many models that all scored near 0.090-0.093, average them all, since averaging many decorrelated rankers usually beats any single pick. Keep featurize as is. Build four rank-normalized prediction vectors on the same feature matrix: (a) the current RandomForestClassifier(300 trees, max_features 0.3), (b) the current 5-seed MLP on the quantile-normal matrix, (c) LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, min_child_samples=10, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed, verbose=-1), and (d) CatBoostClassifier(iterations=600, depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8). Return the equally weighted mean of the four rankdata(p)/len(p) vectors. Watch the budget: the whole job must finish 15 fits inside 10 minutes, so if needed drop CatBoost iterations rather than adding threads.

title: Near-duplicate training molecule removal
spec: Before fitting any model, compute Tanimoto similarity on Morgan radius-2 bits among the training molecules only. Drop any training molecule that has a training neighbour with similarity at least 0.9 and a different label (conflicting near-duplicates), keeping the others. This removes label noise from close analogue pairs. Train all members on the reduced set, and predict on the full test set. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

title: Append RDKit topological path fingerprint counts
spec: Add the RDKit path-based (Daylight-style) topological fingerprint as an extra feature block, which is untried here and captures linear path substructures rather than the circular environments of Morgan or the pharmacophore patterns of Gobbi. In featurize, use rdkit.Chem.rdFingerprintGenerator.GetRDKitFPGenerator(minPath=1, maxPath=6, fpSize=1024) and call GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy on each molecule, cast to float64 and apply np.log1p, then hstack this 1024-column block after the existing descriptor and Gobbi blocks. Keep the RF settings, the 5-seed MLP on the quantile-normal transform, and the 0.5/0.5 rank blend exactly as they are.

title: Deeper, lower-learning-rate LightGBM replaces the RF
spec: LightGBM scored 0.0903 as a third blend member but has never replaced the tree half of the two-member blend, where it would carry more weight. Swap RandomForestClassifier out for LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=1500, learning_rate=0.01, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=5, colsample_bytree=0.2, subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1, reg_lambda=1.0, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed, verbose=-1) fit on the same descriptors + Gobbi feature matrix, and take predict_proba[:, 1] as the tree score. Keep the 5-seed MLP and the 0.5/0.5 rank average unchanged. The very low learning rate with heavy column subsampling is the regime that usually suits a few-thousand-feature, 1300-row fold; confirm the 15 fits finish inside 10 minutes and cut n_estimators if not.

title: Transductive pseudo-label self-training round
spec: Exploit the unlabeled test molecules, which are available inside fit_predict. First fit the current pipeline (RF + 5-seed MLP rank blend) as it stands and obtain blended scores for the test set. Then take the test molecules whose blended score falls in the top 15 percent (pseudo-label 1) or bottom 15 percent (pseudo-label 0), append their feature rows and pseudo-labels to the training matrix with sample weight 0.3 (the original rows get weight 1.0), and refit both the RF (which accepts sample_weight) and the MLPs (for the MLPs, approximate the weighting by simply including the pseudo-labeled rows once). Return the rank-averaged blend from this second round. Keep the two rounds strictly inside fit_predict and make sure total runtime for 15 folds stays under 10 minutes by leaving model sizes unchanged.

title: Three-way tree blend: ExtraTrees + RF + MLP
spec: Keep the current features and MLP exactly as they are, but make the tree side an average of two decorrelated forests instead of one. Fit the existing RandomForestClassifier(300 trees, max_features=0.3, leaf 1, random_state=seed) and additionally an ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=700, max_features=0.5, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed+1). Rank-normalize each of the three prediction vectors (RF, ET, 5-seed MLP) with rankdata/len and combine with weights 0.25 RF, 0.25 ET, 0.50 MLP, so the tree half is split between the two forest types. This tests whether the one good ExtraTrees result is real while hedging against its observed fragility.

title: Bernoulli naive Bayes as third blend member
spec: Add sklearn BernoulliNB (alpha=1.0) trained on binarised Morgan radius-2 bits plus the Gobbi pharmacophore bits (the existing 2048-bit pharmacophore block, binarised at 0.5). Use its predict_proba for class 1, rank-normalise it, and add it to the rank blend with weights 0.25 RF, 0.5 MLP, 0.25 NB (the MLP share stays the largest). Keep the descriptor features out of this model. Keep everything else unchanged.

title: In-fold importance-based feature selection before the MLP
spec: Inside fit_predict, fit a 300-tree RandomForest (seed-controlled) on the training fold only, using the full descriptor plus pharmacophore matrix. Keep the top 300 columns by impurity importance and use only those columns for the quantile transform and the 5-seed MLP. The RF in the blend keeps the full feature set. Selection must use training-fold labels only, so no leakage across folds. Keep the rank blend unchanged.

title: Bootstrap-bagged MLPs
spec: For each of the 8 MLPs, train on a bootstrap resample of the training rows (indices drawn with np.random.RandomState(seed+i)), with early_stopping=True. Average predict_proba across MLPs, then rank-blend with the RF as before. This adds diversity to the MLP half of the blend.

title: Append Avalon fingerprint bits
spec: Add a feature block that has not been tried: the Avalon fingerprint, which is a substructure-plus-path style descriptor distinct from both Morgan and the Gobbi pharmacophore. In featurize, import from rdkit.Avalon import pyAvalonTools and for each molecule compute pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP(mol, nBits=1024), convert it to a dense float vector of length 1024 (loop over the non-zero elements via GetNonzeroElements), apply np.log1p to damp large counts, and hstack it after the existing cleaned descriptor block and Gobbi pharmacophore block. Wrap the per-molecule call in a try/except that returns zeros so a parse failure cannot crash a fold. Leave the RF, MLP and rank blend untouched.

title: Replicate ExtraTrees replacing RF
spec: In fit_predict replace RandomForestClassifier with ExtraTreesClassifier (1000 trees, max_features=0.5, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed), keeping the descriptors+Gobbi features and the 5-seed MLP rank blend 50/50 unchanged. This replicates the earlier 0.0890 result exactly to test whether it is real.

title: Correlation filter on descriptors
spec: After computing the descriptor+Gobbi matrix on the training fold, drop descriptor columns with zero variance. Then drop one of each pair of descriptor columns with absolute Pearson correlation above 0.95 (computed on the train fold only). Apply the same column mask to the test matrix. Use the filtered matrix for both the RF and the MLP.

title: Correlation and variance filter on the descriptor block
spec: Clean up the descriptor block before modeling, since RDKit's descList contains many near-duplicate and near-constant columns that add noise to both members of the blend. Inside fit_predict, compute the filter on the training fold only: drop descriptor columns with training standard deviation below 1e-8, then greedily drop any remaining descriptor column whose absolute Pearson correlation with an already-kept column exceeds 0.95 (iterate columns in order, keep the first of each correlated group). Apply the same column mask to the test fold. Leave the pharmacophore bits untouched, and leave the RF, the 5-seed MLP, and the 0.5/0.5 rank average exactly as they are.

title: Pseudo-label self-training
spec: Fit the current RF+MLP blend once. Then take the test molecules whose blended rank-probability is in the top 20% or bottom 20%, and label them 1 or 0. Add them to the training set with those labels. Refit the RF and MLPs on the augmented set and return the final blend predictions for the test molecules.

title: ExtraTrees plus log1p Morgan counts
spec: Replace the RF with ExtraTreesClassifier (1000 trees, max_features 0.5, min_samples_leaf 1). Also append log1p Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, folded to 1024) to the features for both the ExtraTrees and the MLP inputs. Keep the rank blend 50/50.

title: Transductive quantile fitting on train plus test features
spec: In the MLP branch, fit the QuantileTransformer on the stacked matrix of training and test features (unlabelled test rows are only used to define the marginal distributions; no labels are used), then transform train and test with that fitted transformer. The RF branch keeps raw features. Keep the 5-seed MLP and the rank blend unchanged. This is a transductive preprocessing step that is legitimate because the harness provides the test SMILES at predict time.

title: Fixed-schedule Adam MLP ensemble without early stopping
spec: Replace the early-stopping MLP ensemble with a fixed, gentler optimization schedule, which removes the variance that comes from each seed stopping at a different and noisily chosen epoch. Use 8 MLPClassifier members with hidden_layer_sizes=(256, 64), alpha=1e-2, solver='adam', learning_rate_init=3e-4, batch_size=64, early_stopping=False, max_iter=120, n_iter_no_change=120, tol=0.0 and random_state=seed+i for i in range(8), all fitted on the quantile-normal transformed training fold, and average their predicted probabilities. Suppress ConvergenceWarning. Keep the RF and the 0.5/0.5 rank average exactly as they are. Check runtime: 8 members times 15 folds must fit in 10 minutes, so if the job is slow reduce to 6 members rather than cutting max_iter.

title: Probability averaging with a geometric mean instead of rank averaging
spec: Replace the final rank-averaging with a geometric-mean blend of probabilities. Convert the RF probabilities and the averaged MLP probabilities to logit space (clipped to [1e-4, 1-1e-4]), average the two logits with weights 0.5 each, and map back through the sigmoid. Return the sigmoid output as the score. Keep all members and seeds unchanged. This tests whether keeping calibrated magnitudes helps over pure rank order.
